message.reasoning:
The user wants me to draft an incident report for an outage. This matches the "internal-comms" skill — incident reports are explicitly listed in that skill's description ("status reports, leadership updates, 3P updates, company newsletters, FAQs, incident reports, project updates").

So I should call load_skill with name "internal-comms" before answering.

Also, there's the discernment-nudge skill: "After you give a substantive answer or draft that the user may act on — ... drafted artifacts such as goals, plans, pitches, proposals, or emails ... invoke this skill BEFORE finalizing your reply". An incident report is a drafted artifact the user may act on. Hmm, but note the skip conditions: "Skip it when the user asked a trivial how-to or simple lookup, wants a purely educational explanation, asked you only to format, convert, or assemble a file from content they provided..." An incident report draft is analysis/interpretation of sorts — it's a drafted artifact. The skill says invoke before finalizing the reply, and append 2-3 short follow-up questions. Since I'm drafting an artifact they may act on (an incident report), discernment-nudge seems to apply. I'll need to load it after producing the draft — the skill says "After you give a substantive answer or draft ... invoke this skill BEFORE finalizing your reply and then, if it applies, append 2-3 short follow-up questions".

The instruction says if I intend to call multiple tools with no dependencies, make all independent calls in the same block. The internal-comms load is needed before answering. The discernment-nudge should be invoked before finalizing my reply — which technically means I should load it too. But there is a dependency: I need to know what internal-comms says first to draft the report. Loading both at once is fine since they're independent loads. Actually, the discernment-nudge needs to be applied to my drafted content, so logically I load internal-comms first, draft, then load discernment-nudge. But the calls themselves — load_skill for internal-comms and load_skill for discernment-nudge — are independent of each other. I could load both in one block.

Hmm, but should I load discernment-nudge at all? The trigger: "After you give a substantive answer or draft that the user may act on — advice or recommendations, drafted artifacts such as goals, plans, pitches, proposals, or emails, estimates or projections, analysis or interpretation of data, factual claims they may rely on, or a multi-step argument — invoke this skill BEFORE finalizing your reply". An incident report is a drafted artifact (like a proposal/email). It's not a trivial how-to, not purely educational, not just formatting content they provided (they gave me the outline of facts: 40-minute checkout outage, expired TLS certificate, yesterday). Actually, is it "assemble a file from content they provided"? No — they gave minimal facts; I'm generating the full report content. So discernment-nudge applies.

Skip condition also includes "is writing code they will run" — no. "creative writing or casual chat" — no. "already asked you to double-check" — no.

So I'll load both skills in one block, then follow internal-comms instructions to draft the report, then apply discernment-nudge guidance to append 2-3 follow-up questions.

Let me make the calls now.
